title: Smallest Unique Subarray
summary: Given an integer array, determine the shortest subarray that is not identical to any other subarray in the array.
statement: Given an integer array, determine the shortest subarray that is not identical to any other subarray in the array. Return the length of this unique subarray. Two subarrays are identical if they have the same elements in the same positions and the same length.
constraints: nums is nonempty and may contain up to 100,000 positive integers.
Equal subarrays must have the same length and values at every position.
Return the minimum length of any subarray that occurs exactly once.
reference_solution:
def smallest_unique_subarray(nums):
    n=len(nums);suffixes=list(range(n));rank=list(nums);step=1
    while step<n:
        suffixes.sort(key=lambda start:(rank[start],rank[start+step] if start+step<n else -1))
        next_rank=[0]*n
        for order in range(1,n):
            previous=suffixes[order-1];current=suffixes[order]
            next_rank[current]=next_rank[previous]+((rank[previous],rank[previous+step] if previous+step<n else -1)!=(rank[current],rank[current+step] if current+step<n else -1))
        rank=next_rank
        if rank[suffixes[-1]]==n-1:break
        step*=2
    order=[0]*n
    for position,start in enumerate(suffixes):order[start]=position
    lcp=[0]*max(0,n-1);length=0
    for start in range(n):
        position=order[start]
        if position==n-1:length=0;continue
        other=suffixes[position+1]
        while start+length<n and other+length<n and nums[start+length]==nums[other+length]:length+=1
        lcp[position]=length
        if length:length-=1
    answer=n
    for start in range(n):
        position=order[start];left=lcp[position-1] if position else 0;right=lcp[position] if position<n-1 else 0;shared=max(left,right)
        if shared<n-start:answer=min(answer,shared+1)
    return answer

hints: Every subarray is a prefix of the suffix beginning at the same position.
In suffix-array order, the longest prefix shared with any other suffix is the larger LCP with the two adjacent suffixes.
That suffix needs exactly one more value than its largest adjacent LCP to become unique.
Evaluate this required prefix at every start and take the smallest valid length; a suffix array and Kasai scan avoid enumerating subarrays.
